video_title: The Black Market of Butt Injections

segments.segment_title: The Black Market of Butt Injections
segments.text: When it comes to Brazilian Butt Lifts, sometimes you get what you pay for. This surgery has become the fastest-growing cosmetic procedure in the world, However, it's dangerous. So dangerous that some surgeons are refusing to perform it. But demand for it is growing so fast that some oppertunistic hustlers began offering “affordable” options on social media. Options that have killed dozens of women. One of these shoddy knockoff surgeries included injecting cement into a patient's buttocks. Another operation killed a patient within minutes. So what steps can you take to avoid these backside swindlers? If your butt lift is taking place in a hotel room, that's probably not a good start.

To perform the procedure correctly, doctors use liposuction  to remove fat  from another part of your body, like your abdomen. They filter the fat  to extract the healthy cells it contains, and then inject those cells between the butt muscles and the surrounding skin. The injections require so much precision that even trained physicians might accidentally bypass the subcutaneous area and inject the fat right into the muscle. This will allow the fat to travel to the lungs and heart, causing them to collapse and killing you in minutes. A BBL is dangerous even when perfomed under safe conditions. According to a study published in the Aesthetic Surgery Journal in 2017, 3% of the interviewed surgeons around the world reported experiencing the death of a patient during the procedure. But if you still want that hourglass shape, you should look for an experienced doctor with an impeccable track record. You’ll see what I mean in the next step.

In order to to bypass the whole painful and expensive procedure, some unscrupulous people offer to inject body fillers that in many cases are illegal. Professional filler treatments like Sculptra cost about $6,000 and are performed in medical facilities, while back-alley procedures are touted on social media for less than $1,000 and are performed in hotel rooms or basements. In February of 2022,  the body of Maxine Messam was abandoned in front of a New York City hospital. She was half naked and had injection marks on her butt. Inside her buttocks,  doctors found an unidentified substance that caused her death. To avoid these sad consequences,  spare no expense and turn to trusted professionals.

Some journalists have gone undercover in this reckless business, exposing the con artists that have no medical training and don't even know what ingredients are in the fillers they're injecting into people. “Okay, so mainly collagen. We have aloe vera plant sea weed, vitamin E, fucus... I don’t know how to pronounce it...  So we could google it, if you want. Even butt augmentations using materials that may sound familiar, like silicone, are highly dangerous and illegal in the U.S.

A California doctor was left speechless when he discovered cement inside a patient’s buttocks. The removal was extremely difficult and painful for the patient, but fortunately she survived. If you’re lucky enough to live through the procedure, you'll still need to watch for warning signs afterward. Some patients report experiencing excruciating pain, saying that their silicone injections felt like fire under their skin, If the silicone isn't removed, it can cause sepsis, which is when the body has an extreme and sometimes deadly reaction to a massive infection. If something feels off back there, you better seek medical attention immediately.

Remember, aesthetic trends  are just that: trends. They change sooner rather than later. Having cement injected in your body to fit an Instagram trend doesn’t sound very tempting when you put it like that, does it? If you want to have a strong and attractive shape,  you’re better off sticking to a healthy diet and exercising regularly. That never gets old, right? And speaking of dangerous trends,  have you heard that some TikTokers  are shaving off 60% of their teeth  to get the "perfect" smile?  Yeah, if you want to see what happens  when you expose the pulp of your teeth  on purpose  after watching a TikTok video,  stick around for more How to Survive.
